eventStaff.title: Custom Event Staff Uniforms & Crew Clothing | LF Clothing
eventStaff.description: Custom event staff uniforms, crew clothing and branded jackets for your team. Start with a reference image; LF coordinates samples, production and delivery.
eventStaff.heading: Custom event staff uniforms for your team.
eventStaff.intro: Outfit your hosts, crew and outdoor teams through one supplier contact, with clothing that makes each role easy to recognise while carrying the same event identity. LF brings 20 years of clothing experience to custom event staff uniforms, from adapting existing styles to developing new garments. We manage development, samples and production follow-up so your team can plan the clothing order alongside the event.

sections.heading: One event identity, clothing for each role.
sections.body: Reception staff, exhibition crews and outdoor teams can share your colours and branding while wearing different garments. Coordinate polos, T-shirts, shirts, jackets, tailored pieces and caps according to the work people will do. A host greeting guests may need a different fit and finish from a crew member moving equipment or working outside. Tell us about movement, layering, pockets and identification, and we will help translate those needs into garment details. You can order a single item or plan a range across the whole team.
items: Match each staff role with the garments and layers it needs.
Separate size quantities by item, including any spare clothing you need.
Use shared artwork and colour references for logos and role identification.

sections.heading: Turn your event look into clothing people can wear.
sections.body: Start with a reference photograph, an AI concept, a sketch or a garment you already like. A finished tech pack is not required. LF helps develop the fabric, fit, construction and branding details, then prepares a sample you can assess before production. Use that stage to look at how the garment fits, how the logo reads and whether pockets or layers work for the intended role. Both semi-custom and fully developed garments follow the quality requirements set for your order.
items: Show the details you want to keep and those you want to change.
Check artwork size and position on each garment type.
Approve the sample, materials and order details before bulk production.

sections.heading: Plan from the date your team needs the clothing.
sections.body: Share the required arrival date and destination early, including time to distribute clothing to staff before the event. We build the schedule around sampling, your feedback, material readiness, production and shipping. Specialist production partners make the garments; LF manages development, samples, production follow-up, quality checks and packing. Tell us how you want garments grouped or cartons identified for your crew, so those instructions form part of the order. You have one contact to discuss progress and any changes needed along the way.

faqs.question: Should we customise an existing style or develop a new one?
faqs.answer: If an existing style gives your team the fit and appearance it needs, start with colours, logos or selected detail changes. For a different fabric, silhouette or construction, discuss full development. We explain the work involved and quote for your chosen route; neither route has a standard price or minimum that fits every order.

faqs.question: What do you need to quote our event clothing?
faqs.answer: Send references, quantities by garment, size requirements, artwork, destination and the date staff need their clothing. Minimum quantities depend on the styles, materials, colours and decoration. A simple list is enough to begin, and we will help fill in the garment details needed for a quotation.

faqs.question: When does sampling start, and how is the event schedule set?
faqs.answer: After order confirmation and payment of the sample fee, sampling starts as soon as possible. Clothing samples take 7–12 days. Bulk timing depends on your products, quantities, materials and customisation. We plan production and shipping separately around approvals and your required arrival date before agreeing the schedule.

faqs.question: Can we request fabric reports or garment testing?
faqs.answer: Yes. Tell us which reports or tests your purchasing team needs. Relevant fabric reports can be provided, and custom finished-garment testing can be arranged for an additional fee. We set out the scope and cost beforehand; a fabric report does not by itself certify the finished garment.

corporate.title: Custom Corporate Uniforms & Staff Clothing | LF Clothing
corporate.description: Corporate uniforms for different staff roles, from suits and polos to workwear. Coordinate branding, samples, partner production and related items with LF.
corporate.heading: Corporate uniforms for every role in your company.
corporate.intro: Give each department clothing suited to its work, with coordinated branding and one supplier contact across the range. LF helps company purchasing teams bring suits, polos, workwear and related items into one organised order. With 20 years of clothing experience, we manage garment development, samples and production follow-up, whether you are updating familiar uniforms or creating a new company look.

sections.heading: A consistent company look across different jobs.
sections.body: Reception, service and operational staff can share your brand identity without wearing the same outfit. Coordinate tailored suits, polos and practical workwear using common colour references and artwork, with fabric, fit and garment details suited to each role. Begin with what staff do during their day: greeting visitors, serving customers, moving between locations or working outdoors. This gives the clothing a practical purpose as well as a consistent appearance. Samples let you see how the individual garments work together before you approve production.
items: Group garments by staff role, with quantities and sizes for each item.
Share existing colours, logos and the uniform details staff want to retain.
Identify different layers or garment combinations needed across departments.

sections.heading: Bring clothing and related items into one brief.
sections.body: Send one list of the clothing and accessories you need; LF coordinates the requirements and sets out the available options and schedule for each item. Footwear, caps and other headwear, towels, PPE and construction safety helmets can be included or ordered separately. Use the list to show where branding should match and where a product has a specific operational purpose. PPE and helmet options depend on their intended use, destination market and required standards, with supporting documents and proposed changes assessed for the exact product.
items: Include quantities, dimensions or size requirements for related products.
Add delivery locations and the dates each team needs its items.
Describe how garments should be grouped and cartons identified for distribution.

sections.heading: One contact for samples, production and delivery planning.
sections.body: LF helps turn the brief into garment specifications and samples, giving your purchasing team a clear basis for decisions on fit, appearance and branding. Specialist production partners make the garments, while LF manages development, samples, production follow-up, quality checks and packing. We communicate progress and issues so changes can be discussed before the order moves on. Tell us about different site requirements or planned staff distributions early; these help shape the size breakdown, packing instructions and delivery plan for your range.

faqs.question: Should we update existing uniforms or develop new garments?
faqs.answer: If the current style works well, start with branding, colours or selected detail changes. Full development suits a brief that calls for a different fabric, fit or construction. Both routes follow your quality requirements. Price and minimums depend on the items, materials, quantities and development work, which we explain in the quotation.

faqs.question: Can we start with pictures instead of a technical pack?
faqs.answer: Yes. Reference photos, an AI concept, a sketch or an existing garment are enough to begin. Show what you like and what needs to change. We help develop the practical specification for sampling, including fabric, measurements, garment details and branding.

faqs.question: When does sampling start, and how long does an order take?
faqs.answer: After order confirmation and payment of the sample fee, we start sampling as soon as possible. Clothing samples take 7–12 days. Bulk timing depends on each product, quantity and customisation, including approvals and material readiness. We set out the item schedules and shipping separately against your required arrival dates.

faqs.question: Can our purchasing team request test reports?
faqs.answer: Yes. Relevant fabric reports can be provided, and finished-garment testing can be arranged to your requirements. Tests on custom finished garments carry an additional fee, with the scope and cost set out beforehand. PPE and other protective items need evidence for the particular product and intended use.

workwear.title: Custom Workwear Manufacturer in China | LF Clothing
workwear.description: Custom workwear for company teams. LF manages development and sampling, with production organised through specialist manufacturing partners in China.
workwear.heading: Custom workwear built around your team’s daily work.
workwear.intro: Equip your staff with jackets, work trousers and coveralls suited to their jobs, while keeping company branding consistent across the range. LF gives purchasing teams one contact for garment development, samples and production follow-up. With 20 years of clothing experience, we support familiar workwear with selected changes as well as fully developed designs for different operational roles.

sections.heading: Start with how your team works.
sections.body: Tell us what staff carry, how they move and where their clothing gets the most wear. Those details guide the pocket layout, fit, fabric and construction. Work trousers need attention to the waistband, rise, leg shape and closures; jackets and coveralls need room for reach, movement and the layers worn underneath. Include expected washing conditions and any reinforcement needs. These practical details help turn a visual reference into workwear that addresses the tasks you describe.
items: Place pockets around the tools and everyday items staff need to carry.
Describe working positions and any layers.
Share fabric preferences, washing requirements and areas that need attention.

sections.heading: Keep what works and improve the details.
sections.body: Bring a current jacket, trouser or coverall and tell us what staff like about it. You may want to retain a familiar fit while changing the colour, branding or selected details, or develop different materials and construction. A reference photo, sketch or AI concept is also enough to start; LF helps turn it into a practical specification and sample. Both approaches follow your quality requirements. Use the sample to assess fit, access and appearance before approving production.

sections.heading: Keep production connected to the approved sample.
sections.body: Specialist production partners make the garments, with LF managing development, samples and production follow-up. The approved sample and specification guide checks on measurements, materials, seams, closures, logos, quantities and packing. We follow progress and communicate issues through your supplier contact. Relevant fabric reports can be provided, and custom finished-garment tests can be arranged for an additional fee. Include testing needs in the initial brief so the scope and cost can form part of the quotation.

sections.heading: Plan the order by garment and staff group.
sections.body: One workwear range can cover several departments, each with its own garment combination and size quantities. List jackets and trousers separately, even when they form a set, and add artwork, destinations and required arrival dates. Tell us if packing needs to identify particular teams or locations. LF coordinates those details alongside the clothing, giving purchasing staff one place to discuss the order. Quantities, materials and customisation determine the minimums and price for each item.

faqs.question: Do we need full development for a conventional workwear order?
faqs.answer: No. If a familiar style already fits the job, start with logo application and selected colour or detail changes. For a different fabric, fit, pocket layout or construction, discuss the development needed. We explain the options and cost from your reference and quantities; a new design is not required for every order.

faqs.question: Can different departments wear different garments with the same branding?
faqs.answer: Yes. Shared artwork and colour references can connect jackets, trousers, coveralls and other staff clothing across your teams. Each garment can retain the details needed for its role. Send the staff groups and garment quantities together so we can plan the range and samples as one order.

faqs.question: When do sampling and bulk production begin?
faqs.answer: After order confirmation and payment of the sample fee, sampling starts as soon as possible. Clothing samples take 7–12 days. Bulk production follows approval of the sample, materials and order details. Timing depends on the products, quantities and customisation; production and shipping are planned against your required arrival date.

faqs.question: What if our workwear needs protective performance?
faqs.answer: Share the intended use, destination market and required standards at the start. We assess the garment, materials and testing needed for those requirements. Any custom garment tests are quoted separately. The finished garment needs its own supporting evidence; a fabric report alone does not establish certification.
